## Who Developed R?

- Developed at U Auckland by [Ross Ihaka](https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/~ihaka/) & [Robert Gentleman](https://hsph.harvard.edu/profile/robert-gentleman/)
    + Rewrote the language `S` [@chambers1977computational]
- v1.0.0 released in Feb 2000
- Packages are hosted on the Comprehensive R Archive Network ([CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org))
    + This is where `install.packages()` looks
- CRAN packages are thoroughly tested across multiple platforms
- Cover diverse fields (finance, ecology, psychology, data wrangling etc)
- No formal versioning across packages

## The Bioconductor Project

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column}

- Robert Gentleman is a bioinformatician $\implies$ understood key needs of the field
- Started developing the Bioconductor Project in 2001 [@Gentleman2004-sd]
    + First official release v1.0 in May 2002 (R v1.5)

## The Bioconductor Project {.slide-only .unlisted}
    
- Core data structures for genomic data as *core packages*
    + Sequence information, genomic co-ordinates etc
    + Specific file-types (bam files, bed files, gtf files)
- Core structures heavily used between packages
    + Strong dependency between packages
- Bi-annual releases $\implies$ *all packages released synchronously*
    + Install as an ecosystem of packages
    + Tied to (and tested on) specific version of R
    + Currently at Bioc release `r BiocManager::version()`


## Common Data Structures

For a microrray/RNA-Seq dataset we have three primary data objects

1. Sample annotations and metadata
2. Gene-Level information
3. Expression measurements (counts, fluoresence etc)

## Common Data Structures {.slide-only .unlisted}

A matrix of gene-level counts

```{r}
options(width = 100)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
data(airway, package="airway")
assay(airway, "counts")[1:10, 1:6]
```

::: {.incremental}
- How do we store information about each sample?
- And each gene?
:::

## Common Data Structures {.slide-only .unlisted}

Sample information might look like

```{r}
colData(airway)[1:6, 1:8]
```

::: {.incremental}
- Fragment length, treatment, cell line
- Sequencing, experiment & sample IDs
:::

## Common Data Structures {.slide-only .unlisted}

Gene information might look like

```{r}
rowData(airway)[1:10, c(2, 4:8)]
```

## Common Data Structures {.slide-only .unlisted}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width='55%'}

![](assets/se.png)

:::
::: {.column width='45%'}
- The `SummarizedExperiment` class [@Morgan2026]
- Samples are the columns $\implies$ `colData`
- Genes are the rows $\implies$ `rowData`
- Optional `metadata`
- Everything in one object

:::
::::

## Common Data Structures {.slide-only .unlisted}

- The Digital Gene Expression List (`DGEList`) is similar
- Used by `edgeR` for RNA-Seq analysis [@Chen2025]

::: {.fragment}
- `SummarizedExperiment` objects can be extended
    + `DESeq2` [@Love2014]use a `DESeqDataSet`
    + Tree-based relationships
    + `SingleCellExperiment` etc
    
:::

## Installing Bioconductor Packages

- The package `BiocManager` installs from Bioconductor and CRAN
    + Hosted itself on CRAN `install.packages("BiocManager")`
- Then use to install from either repository

```
library(BiocManager)
install("DESeq2")
```

## The Bioconductor Ecosystem

- Standardised core object structures used widely with ecosystem
    + Heavily relies on the `S4` class system
- Strongly interdependent packages
- Bioconductor Core Team ensure stable build testing, new submissions etc
- Strong focus on community support for users & developers
    + Several key Bioc developers in Adelaide & Australia
- Regional conferences, workshops, seminar series etc
